RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 15

The gender composition of an interview panel is not evidence of bias or unlawful discrimination. In civil service hiring, panels are typically assembled based on seniority, role relevance, and availability. The successful candidate held relevant postgraduate qualifications and international project leadership experience, which may have aligned more closely with the ministry's specific strategic needs.

Alleging bias based solely on the panel’s gender without concrete evidence—such as procedural irregularities, scoring discrepancies, or biased remarks—is unfounded and could significantly damage your professional reputation. Instead, send a polite follow-up requesting your competency scores and constructive feedback to understand how the panel evaluated your interview.
